description:
## Goal

Make the result of fz-kdt.68 total. If measured per-answer precision does not repay its cost, delete the already-landed engine-wide per-derivation substrate rather than retaining latent complexity and hot-path overhead. If the experiment passes and a production multi-derivation consumer lands, close this ticket without code.

## Evidence

Every production JobEffects currently leaves derivations empty and publishes only DerivationId::SOLE. Nevertheless scheduler claims, reads, finality, publisher identity, rosters, and completion plumbing are derivation-granular. The parked semantic consumer previously measured a 6–10 percent regression. fz-kdt.68 owns the new A/B decision.

## Refuted-path deletion

- DerivationId and Publisher wrappers where sole job identity suffices.
- JobDerivation rosters and per-derivation dependency/claim maps.
- Sole-derivation vector construction, reported-roster collection, publisher hashing/cloning, withdrawal plumbing, telemetry, tests, and documentation.
- Experiment-only counters and proof fixtures after the removal is established.

## Proof

1. Let fz-kdt.68 complete its measured decision.
2. If refuted, first pin the single-answer scheduler behavior, then collapse the data model back to job-owned reads/claims/finality.
3. Prove identical current/settled movement, retraction, blocking, rebasing, wake attribution, semantic facts, products, artifacts, and runtime output.
4. Require reduced allocations/hash operations/formula cost by causal or allocator counters; remove probes.
5. Run randomized scheduler differential tests, full library, fixture matrix, determinism, formatting, and strict clippy.

Do not keep generic multi-answer infrastructure without a production consumer and measured benefit.
title: Delete dormant per-derivation scheduler machinery if the precision experiment is refuted
